Native phase heading: `## Phase <digits>` matched case-sensitively at column 0, spaces or tabs as separators.
Native title: the heading text after the number with the leading run of spaces and `-`, em dash or `:` separators removed.
A phase section runs from its heading to the next level-2 heading (or end of file); trailing blank lines are kept in the raw slice.
Native criteria block heading: `### Acceptance criteria` (case-sensitive prefix match); the block ends at the next line starting with `###`.
Checkbox syntax for all formats: optional indent, `-`, optional spaces, `[ ]`, `[x]`, `[X]` or `[]`, then the text.
Native criteria are only the checkbox lines inside the acceptance-criteria block.
Native error `spec has zero phases (need at least one "## Phase <N>")`.
Native error `phase <n> (<raw heading text>) has no "### Acceptance criteria" block`; the block may be empty of checkboxes and still validate.
Error `duplicate phase number: <n>` (all formats); a duplicate also yields the non-contiguous message.
Error `non-contiguous phases: <b> follows <a> (must ascend by 1)` (all formats); the first number is free (0, 1 or any).
Native error order: per-phase missing-criteria messages first in scan order, then duplicate/contiguity messages.
Spec Kit phase heading: `## Phase <digits>` with optional `:` and free title text.
Spec Kit criteria: every checkbox line with non-empty text anywhere in the phase section (not only `T###` lines, and under any `###` subheading).
Spec Kit priority form: `## P<N>` / `## p<N>` headings with optional `-`, em dash or `:` separator.
Explicit `## Phase N` headings win; the priority form is used only when no explicit phase exists.
Priority form: only sections that hold task checkboxes become phases; they are numbered contiguously in document order starting at the first priority number; repeated priorities are valid.
Priority form: level-2 sections after the last task-bearing group are appended to EVERY phase's section as shared constraints.
Priority form title keeps the priority label (the whole heading text after `##`).

Phase shape digest: first 16 hex of sha256 over compact JSON `[n, title, [criteria]]` with whitespace runs collapsed; ticking a checkbox never changes it.

Feature slug: an OpenSpec change uses its change directory basename; a spec inside a `.specify` project uses its feature directory basename; anything else, or a spec at the project root, is `default`.
Slug sanitising: runs outside `A-Za-z0-9._-` collapse to `-`, leading/trailing `-` trimmed; an empty result falls back to `default`.
The `.specify` project root is found by walking upward from the spec's directory.
Spec Kit context order: constitution, spec, plan, `contract:<stem>` (sorted), data-model, research, quickstart, `checklist:<stem>` (sorted); each only when the file exists.
The constitution is context only when the spec is inside a `.specify` project.
OpenSpec context order: `proposal`, `delta-spec:<name>` (recursive, sorted), `design`, then `current-spec:<name>` for each delta with a matching `openspec/specs/` file.
Context budget default is 24000 characters across all context documents.
Per-document floor is 1200 characters: a document that would get less is dropped, unless the whole document fits.
Budget allocation walks documents in priority order, giving each the smaller of its size, a fair share (at least the floor) and what remains; leftover cascades forward.
A truncated context document ends with the marker `… (context truncated at line boundary) …`.
Truncation cuts at a line boundary (hard cut only for one over-long line) and closes an unbalanced code fence.
Each context block starts `## Context: <name> (read-only background, NOT a gate) — <path>`; blocks are joined by a blank line.
The native format renders no context.
Ticking handles only `speckit-tasks` with explicit `## Phase N` headings and `openspec-change`; native specs and the `## P<N>` priority form are left untouched (0 ticked).
An unticked line is a checkbox `[ ]` or `[]` followed by non-empty text; it becomes `[x]`. Already ticked lines and empty boxes are untouched.
Only lines inside phase N's section are ticked; any other level-2 heading ends the section. Every unticked checkbox there is ticked, not only task-id lines.
Line endings and every other byte are preserved (the file is read and written with `newline=""`).
A tick rewrites the spec atomically through `<spec>.tick.<pid>.tmp`, copies the file mode, then `os.replace`; nothing is written when no line changed.
The five vendored templates are read at run time by the linter when the source has no `.specify/templates/`; they are an unchanged copy of Spec Kit's templates at a recorded commit.
